Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee, ME31

FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Optical and Mathematical Instruments Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1977 for telescopic type tripods only and was revised in 1986 to include the requirements of fixed leg type tripods also. Since International Standard 1S0 12858-2:1999 `Optics and optical instruments -- Ancillary devices for geodetic instruments : Part 2 Tripods' has been published for telescopic type tripods, the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard felt the necessity to adopt the International Standard. Accordingly this second revision is taken up to cover only fixed leg type tripods. Surveying fixed leg type tripod commonly known as stand is an essential accesso~ required for mounting of plane table tops, levels, targets and other surveying instruments in topographical non-precision surveying work. The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the results of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revise@'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

Indian Standard TRIPODS FOR SURVEYING INSTRUMENTS FIXED LEG TYPE -- SPECIFICATION ( Second Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard covers the requirements of fixed leg type tripods for surveying instruments. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed below contain provisions, which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and.parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated below:

Brass and gun metal of non-magnetic variety may also be used. 4 GENERALREQ~ 4.1 The legs of the tripods shall be fixed type. 4.2 The height as measured vertically fi-omthe top of the tripod head to shoe shall be between 1.5 m and 1.6 m. 4.3 The tripods shall be rigid, robust and as light as possible. 5 DIMENSIONAL REQUIREMENTS AND CONSTRUCTIONAL

5.1 The main dimensions and various parts of the tripods shall be as shown in Fig. 1. The other dimensions shall be at the discretion of the manufacturers. 5.2 The tripod clamp shall be fitted into the tripod head in a manner, which would prevent it from being lost. The dimensions of the tripod clamp shall be as shown in Fig. 2. 5.2.1 Optional If agreed to between the manufacturer and the user, the following threads may also be provided in the tripod clamps in addition to M 16 threads as specified in Fig. 2. a) Diameter 14 mm, pitch 2 mm; and b) Diameter 15 mm, pitch 1.5 mm. 5.3 A protecting cap made of plastic or metal shall be fastened to the tripod head by means of tripod clamp. 5.4 The tripod clamp shall have a hole of about 9 rnm in diameter in order to make use of optical plummets. 5.5 The plumb-bob attachment shall be able to be fitted into tripod clamp for centering the instrument. 5.6 A circular bubble conforming to IS 1632 shall be provided on the tripod head. The sensitivity of the circular bubble shall be 25 + 5 min over 2 mm run. 5.7 The legs shall be made of wood. 5.8 The shoes of the tripod stand shall be made of steel and shall be sharply pointed out at the end so that tripod legs are firmly inserted into the ground. 1

3 MATERIAL

3.1 The surveying fixed leg type tripods shall be made fi-omone of the following species of timber:
Trade-Mark Botanical Name Tectona grandis Linn. f. Dalbergia sissoo Roxb. Artocarpus Morus sp. Betula sp. Grevillea robusta A. Cunn. hirsuta Lamk

Teak Sissoo Aini Mulberry Birch Silver oak

3.2 The timber used for the tripods shall be thoroughly seasoned, radially sawn and shall conform to the requirements of IS 287. It shall be free from defects such as knots, cracks, shakes, insect attack, decay, etc. 3.3 The material for the metallic portion shall be hard and preferably aluminiurn alloy conforming to designation 19000 of IS 737. All dimensions in millimetres. FIG.2 DIMENSIONS FOR TRIPOD CLAMP 5.9 A long leather belt shall be provided with one of the legs for carrying the tripods. Rot proof canvas of any shade may also be used as an alternative. 5.10 A leather or rot proof canvas strap shall also be provided with one of the legs for closing the tripods. 5.11 The tripod shall be stable against strong winds. 5.12 A leather or canvas case shall be provided on the inner side of one of the legs for keeping the accessories supplied with the tripod. 6 ACCESSORIES 6.1 Key for tightening the screws of the tripod stand, shall be supplied with every unit. 6.2 Plumb-bob made of brass or leaded brass having a mass of 100 g with a hard tip may also be supplied with the tripod stand if desired by the purchaser. 7 FINISH The tripod shall be painted with weather-resistant varnish or paint, preferably with a high contrast colour. 3 8 TESTS The tripod shall conform to the requirements given in 3 to 7. 9 MARKING 9.1 The tripod shall be marked with the manufacturer's name or trade-mark, serial number and the year of manufacture. 9.2 -BIS Certification Marking The tripod may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 9.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which a Iicence for the use of Standard Mark may be granted to the manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 10 PACKIN.G The tripods shall be suitably packed for transit.

Bureau of Indian Standards BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Zndian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country. Copyright BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. Review of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'. This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc : No. ME31 (665).
